package.name: pimesh_instruments
package.description:
The tests for the Python instruments in tools/ that decide what a gate prints.
Three gates are closed by a number a Python script computes rather than by a node: gates/calibration.sh by tools/calib_straightness.py, gates/mesh.sh by tools/mesh_render.py, and gates/keypoints.sh by tools/orb_reference.py — which is the predecessor's ORB algorithm reimplemented, and therefore the only outside opinion in this workspace about whether the corners mean anything. A gate's instrument needs its own tests for the same reason the gate does, and two of the ways orb_reference.py can be wrong move its number *up*, so the failure is a gate that passes for the wrong reason.
It exists because those three suites were filed under pimesh_bringup until #14's P5, where they had nothing to do with launch files, config or RViz — they were there because bringup was the package with a Python test harness. This package is that harness and nothing else: no nodes, no headers, no install step. It builds on both machines so that gates/test.sh can go on asserting the same suites at both ends, and it needs no camera, no bag and no GPU — every one of these is synthetic by construction, which is what lets them run at all.
